Package com.im.njams.sdk.settings

Class HierarchicalSettings

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.im.njams.sdk.settings.HierarchicalSettings
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    ClientSettings, Iterable<Map.Entry<String,​String>>
    public final class HierarchicalSettings
extends Object
implements ClientSettings
    A ClientSettings that composes an ordered list of named layers. Each read operation consults the layers in order and returns the result from the first layer that contains the requested key. Write operations (put(String, String), ClientSettings.putAll(Map), addSecureProperties(Set)) are applied exclusively to the base layer supplied to from(ClientSettings).

    Construction goes through a fluent builder: 

    
 ClientSettings settings = HierarchicalSettings.from(myDefaults).withName("defaults")
     .andThen(fileSettings).withName(fileName)
     .andThenSystemProperties().withPrefixFilter("njams.")
     .andThenEnvironmentVariables().withPrefixFilter("NJAMS_")
     .build();
    Layer names appear in printPropertiesWithoutPasswords(Logger) output to attribute each entry to its source. Each layer carries its own secured-keys configuration; a value is masked based on the source layer's tokens, not on a global union.

        public static HierarchicalSettings.Builder from​(ClientSettings base)

      • from

        public static HierarchicalSettings.Builder from​(Map<String,​String> base)
        Convenience factory that wraps the given map in ClientSettings.from(Map) and uses it as the base layer.

        The map must accept write operations. Writes through the hierarchical settings are dispatched to the base layer, so an immutable or unmodifiable map would fail the first time a property is set. To catch this early, the map is probed with a put/remove of a reserved sentinel key at this call; if the probe throws any exception (the JDK's UnsupportedOperationException, an implementation- specific IllegalStateException, a custom security check, etc.), an IllegalArgumentException is thrown with the original cause attached.

        Parameters:
        base - the writable map to use as the base layer; must not be null
        Returns:
        a builder for adding further layers
        Throws:
        NullPointerException - if base is null
        IllegalArgumentException - if the writability probe on base throws any exception

      • from

        public static HierarchicalSettings.Builder from​(Properties base)
        Convenience factory that wraps the given properties in ClientSettings.from(Properties) and uses them as the base layer.

        The properties must accept write operations. Writes through the hierarchical settings are dispatched to the base layer, so a Properties subclass that rejects mutations would fail the first time a property is set. To catch this early, the properties are probed with a setProperty/remove of a reserved sentinel key at this call; if the probe throws any exception (the JDK's UnsupportedOperationException, an implementation-specific IllegalStateException, a custom security check, etc.), an IllegalArgumentException is thrown with the original cause attached.

        Parameters:
        base - the writable properties to use as the base layer; must not be null
        Returns:
        a builder for adding further layers
        Throws:
        NullPointerException - if base is null
        IllegalArgumentException - if the writability probe on base throws any exception

      • fromEmpty

        public static HierarchicalSettings.Builder fromEmpty()
        Starts a new hierarchical settings chain with an in-memory, initially empty base layer. The base is a ClientSettings backed by a fresh LinkedHashMap; writes through the resulting hierarchical settings are stored there and discarded when the instance becomes unreachable. The base layer is named <in-memory> by default; override with HierarchicalSettings.Builder.withName(String) if needed.
        Returns:
        a builder for adding further layers

      • keySet

        public default Set<String> keySet()
        Returns the set of registered keys. The default implementation walks the iterator; implementations are expected to override this with a direct lookup against the backing storage for efficiency. Filtering implementations must apply the key filter so that only visible keys appear in the returned set.
        Returns:
        an unmodifiable set of the registered keys

      • getIntWithDeprecationWarning

        public default int getIntWithDeprecationWarning​(String expectedKey,
                                                int defaultValue,
                                                String deprecatedKey)
        Same as getInt(String, int) with deprecated-key fallback. The deprecated key is tried only if expectedKey is not present; a deprecation warning is logged when the fallback is used. If neither key is present (or both yield unparseable values), the default is returned.
        Parameters:
        expectedKey - the expected (current) key
        defaultValue - the value to return when neither key is present or both values are invalid
        deprecatedKey - deprecated key to try if the expected key does not exist
        Returns:
        the parsed integer or defaultValue

      • getPropertyWithAlternativeKey

        public default String getPropertyWithAlternativeKey​(String expectedKey,
                                                    String defaultValue,
                                                    String alternativeKey)
        Returns the value for expectedKey if present. Otherwise, if alternativeKey is present, its value is returned. If neither key is present, defaultValue is returned.

        Unlike getPropertyWithDeprecationWarning(String, String, String), no warning is logged: both keys are equally valid, permanent spellings of the same setting, and neither is deprecated. This is intended for settings whose primary key also happens to be a prefix of other settings keys, which makes the primary key impossible to express in some hierarchical configuration formats (e.g. YAML); the alternative key gives such sources a collision-free way to set the same value.

        Parameters:
        expectedKey - the primary key
        defaultValue - the value to return when neither key is present
        alternativeKey - an equally valid alternative key to try if expectedKey is not present
        Returns:
        the resolved value, or defaultValue if neither key is present
